newsitem.title: UK: UK's Lang rejects shake-up of competition bodies.
newsitem.headline: UK's Lang rejects shake-up of competition bodies.

text.p: Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang on Tuesday rejected calls for a shake-up of institutions which police the government's competition policy, saying the existing structure was "clear and rational".
Making a speech to a London conference on competition, Lang said: "The well-ordered distribution of roles which our system entails is one of its very key strengths."

Under the existing structure, the Office of Fair Trading (OFT) keeps watch on monopolies, mergers, restrictive agreements and anti-competitive practices while the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) investigate matters referred to it by the OFT or by Lang himself.

Some critics have argued for a merger of the two bodies. However, Lang said: "There is a clear and rational delineation between the tasks entrusted to the OFT, the MMC and the DTI (Department of Trade and Industry)."
"I see no need to interfere with this structure. It is this division of responsibility which is crucial to the ability of our system to get to the heart of the key public interest issues."

Lang also said that he did not have "a closed mind" on the question of whether to introduce a prohibition of market power into British law along the lines of that already enshrined in European Union competition policy.

"While such a system has the advantage of strongly deterring abuse, I am not yet convinced that this outweighs the disadvantage that it could act as a disincentive towards genuine competition and innovation," Lang added. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
